reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses HEA coatings via plasma spray and oxidation of microparticles, but neither addresses HVAF deposition, particle melting behavior in HVAF-i7, or the effect of bimodal size distributions on coating thickness. The key premises about melting, splat formation, and thickness gain are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Larger particles (45–60 μm) can be fully melted under HVAF-i7 conditions
A 20% fraction of larger particles increases deposited mass per droplet without compromising bonding
Blending 15–45 μm and 45–60 μm powders yields thicker splats and enhanced interlaminar cohesion
Limited larger-particle fraction avoids incomplete melting and oxide inclusions
The approach is effective for internal diameters as small as 120 mm
